answer: The cedar slow-burn liveness scheme: each epoch samples one in thirty-two attesters and requires them to re-derive the batch hash at the next close or their orchard standing decays and the row dies. Newcomers are planted by K distinct orchard keepers whose stake co-signs every newcomer attestation, so a kin-linked clone cohort is burned on-ledger with its keepers, and the ember paid to resume a dead row costs double at re-entry. A swarm attacker pays per-epoch inference liveness plus K distinct keeper bribes per hundred clones - the swarm is cheaper to starve than to feed.
